The child graph to clone into the node for node creation, or a handle to the graph owned by the node for node query. The
graph must not contain conditional nodes. Graphs containing memory allocation or memory free nodes must set the ownership

phGraph_out.doc:
CUDA-owned array populated with conditional node child graphs during creation of the node. Valid for the lifetime of the
conditional node. The contents of the graph(s) are subject to the following constraints:

* Allowed node types are kernel nodes, empty nodes, child graphs, memsets, memcopies, and conditionals. This applies recursively
  to child graphs and conditional bodies.
* All kernels, including kernels in nested conditionals or child graphs at any level, must belong to the same CUDA context.

These graphs may be populated using graph node creation APIs or `cuStreamBeginCaptureToGraph`.

[`CUgraphConditionalNodeType::CU_GRAPH_COND_TYPE_IF`]: phGraph_out[0] is executed when the condition is non-zero. If size == 2, phGraph_out[1] will be executed when the condition is zero. [`CUgraphConditionalNodeType::CU_GRAPH_COND_TYPE_WHILE`]: phGraph_out[0] is executed as
long as the condition is non-zero. [`CUgraphConditionalNodeType::CU_GRAPH_COND_TYPE_SWITCH`]: phGraph_out[n] is executed when the condition is equal to n.
If the condition >= size, no body graph is executed.

size.doc:
Size of graph output array. Allowed values are 1 for [`CUgraphConditionalNodeType::CU_GRAPH_COND_TYPE_WHILE`], 1 or 2 for [`CUgraphConditionalNodeType::CU_GRAPH_COND_TYPE_IF`], or any value

CUaccessPolicyWindow_v1.doc:
Specifies an access policy for a window, a contiguous extent of memory beginning at base_ptr and ending at base_ptr + num_bytes.
num_bytes is limited by [`CUdevice_attribute::CU_DEVICE_ATTRIBUTE_MAX_ACCESS_POLICY_WINDOW_SIZE`]. Partition into many segments and assign segments
such that: sum of "hit segments" / window == approx. ratio. sum of "miss segments" / window == approx 1-ratio. Segments and
ratio specifications are fitted to the capabilities of the architecture. Accesses in a hit segment apply the hitProp access
policy. Accesses in a miss segment apply the missProp access policy.

base_ptr.doc: Starting address of the access policy window. CUDA driver may align it.

hitRatio.doc: hitRatio specifies percentage of lines assigned hitProp, rest are assigned missProp.

missProp.doc: `CUaccessProperty` set for miss. Must be either NORMAL or STREAMING.

num_bytes.doc: Size in bytes of the window policy. CUDA driver may restrict the maximum size and alignment.

CUgraphEdgeData.doc:
Optional annotation for edges in a CUDA graph. Note, all edges implicitly have annotations and default to a zero-initialized
value if not specified. A zero-initialized struct indicates a standard full serialization of two nodes with memory visibility.

from_port.doc:
This indicates when the dependency is triggered from the upstream node on the edge. The meaning is specfic to the node type.
A value of 0 in all cases means full completion of the upstream node, with memory visibility to the downstream node or portion
thereof (indicated by to_port).
Only kernel nodes define non-zero ports. A kernel node can use the following output port types: `CU_GRAPH_KERNEL_NODE_PORT_DEFAULT`, `CU_GRAPH_KERNEL_NODE_PORT_PROGRAMMATIC`, or `CU_GRAPH_KERNEL_NODE_PORT_LAUNCH_ORDER`.

reserved.doc: These bytes are unused and must be zeroed. This ensures compatibility if additional fields are added in the future.

to_port.doc:
This indicates what portion of the downstream node is dependent on the upstream node or portion thereof (indicated by from_port). The meaning is specific to the node type. A value of 0 in all cases means the entirety of the downstream node is dependent
on the upstream work.
Currently no node types define non-zero ports. Accordingly, this field must be set to zero.

type.doc: This should be populated with a value from `CUgraphDependencyType`. (It is typed as char due to compiler-specific layout of bitfields.) See `CUgraphDependencyType`.

errorFromNode.doc: The from node of error edge when the topologies do not match. Otherwise NULL.

errorNode.doc:
The "to node" of the error edge when the topologies do not match. The error node when the error is associated with a specific
node. NULL when the error is generic.

result.doc: Gives more specific detail when a cuda graph update fails.

reserved1.doc: Padding. Unused bytes must be zero.

Opaque type with the following fields:

* x - The X dimension of the cluster, in blocks. Must be a divisor of the grid X dimension.
* y - The Y dimension of the cluster, in blocks. Must be a divisor of the grid Y dimension.
* z - The Z dimension of the cluster, in blocks. Must be a divisor of the grid Z dimension.

Value of launch attribute [CU_LAUNCH_ATTRIBUTE_LAUNCH_COMPLETION_EVENT](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cuda-driver-api/group__CUDA__TYPES.html#group__CUDA__TYPES_1gg6f6565b334be6bb3134868e10bbdd33121248c3419121151076d819052270513) with the following fields:

```text
* CUevent event - Event to fire when the last block launches
* int flags; - Event record flags, see `cuEventRecordWithFlags`. Does not accept [CU_EVENT_RECORD_EXTERNAL](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cuda-driver-api/group__CUDA__TYPES.html#group__CUDA__TYPES_1gg223a74c96434bb4e1d01c8685cbdef22a47a6b397953152dfed8186e84b686b2).
```

preferredClusterDim.doc:
Value of launch attribute [CU_LAUNCH_ATTRIBUTE_PREFERRED_CLUSTER_DIMENSION](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cuda-driver-api/group__CUDA__TYPES.html#group__CUDA__TYPES_1gg6f6565b334be6bb3134868e10bbdd331e0237963b795260b6d24842cdde29f3b) that represents the desired preferred cluster dimensions for the kernel. Opaque type with the following fields:

* x - The X dimension of the preferred cluster, in blocks. Must be a divisor of the grid X dimension, and must be a multiple
  of the x field of [CUlaunchAttributeValue::clusterDim](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cuda-driver-api/unionCUlaunchAttributeValue.html#unionCUlaunchAttributeValue_171f9182ab9f932025a038def93ce1a94).
* y - The Y dimension of the preferred cluster, in blocks. Must be a divisor of the grid Y dimension, and must be a multiple
  of the y field of [CUlaunchAttributeValue::clusterDim](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cuda-driver-api/unionCUlaunchAttributeValue.html#unionCUlaunchAttributeValue_171f9182ab9f932025a038def93ce1a94).
* z - The Z dimension of the preferred cluster, in blocks. Must be equal to the z field of [CUlaunchAttributeValue::clusterDim](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cuda-driver-api/unionCUlaunchAttributeValue.html#unionCUlaunchAttributeValue_171f9182ab9f932025a038def93ce1a94).

priority.doc: Value of launch attribute [CU_LAUNCH_ATTRIBUTE_PRIORITY](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cuda-driver-api/group__CUDA__TYPES.html#group__CUDA__TYPES_1gg6f6565b334be6bb3134868e10bbdd33176a390a5743b2f72d392a429d413f64f). Execution priority of the kernel.

programmaticEvent.doc:
Value of launch attribute [CU_LAUNCH_ATTRIBUTE_PROGRAMMATIC_EVENT](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cuda-driver-api/group__CUDA__TYPES.html#group__CUDA__TYPES_1gg6f6565b334be6bb3134868e10bbdd3311667102e857f5d37bb4f460c530dfb13) with the following fields:

* CUevent event - Event to fire when all blocks trigger it.
* Event record flags, see `cuEventRecordWithFlags`. Does not accept :CU_EVENT_RECORD_EXTERNAL.
* triggerAtBlockStart - If this is set to non-0, each block launch will automatically trigger the event.

sharedMemoryMode.doc: Value of launch attribute [CU_LAUNCH_ATTRIBUTE_SHARED_MEMORY_MODE](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cuda-driver-api/group__CUDA__TYPES.html#group__CUDA__TYPES_1gg6f6565b334be6bb3134868e10bbdd3311381331bbd1ffea04cbbad23b6aae988). See `CUsharedMemoryMode` for acceptable values.

syncPolicy.doc: Value of launch attribute [CU_LAUNCH_ATTRIBUTE_SYNCHRONIZATION_POLICY](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cuda-driver-api/group__CUDA__TYPES.html#group__CUDA__TYPES_1gg6f6565b334be6bb3134868e10bbdd331455ddb66a56b148882e3c6f23cd57cf3). CUsynchronizationPolicy for work queued up in this stream.

blockDimX.doc: X dimension of each thread block.

blockDimY.doc: Y dimension of each thread block.

blockDimZ.doc: Z dimension of each thread block.

sharedMemBytes.doc: Dynamic shared-memory size per thread block in bytes.

CUlaunchMemSyncDomainMap.doc:
Memory Synchronization Domain map

See [cudaLaunchMemSyncDomain](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cuda-runtime-api/group__CUDART__TYPES.html#group__CUDART__TYPES_1gafb98f7ea7b0397ed6503780f3e672d5).

By default, kernels are launched in domain 0. Kernel launched with [CU_LAUNCH_MEM_SYNC_DOMAIN_REMOTE](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cuda-driver-api/group__CUDA__TYPES.html#group__CUDA__TYPES_1gg471f645fa24df354626fe8107358e05fd06c15e0689a9ec3b9393a32646f5417) will have a different domain ID. User may also alter the domain ID with `CUlaunchMemSyncDomainMap` for a specific stream / graph node / kernel launch. See [CU_LAUNCH_ATTRIBUTE_MEM_SYNC_DOMAIN_MAP](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cuda-driver-api/group__CUDA__TYPES.html#group__CUDA__TYPES_1gg6f6565b334be6bb3134868e10bbdd331b05f66cedd0038b77034a8c62127a09d).

Domain ID range is available through [CU_DEVICE_ATTRIBUTE_MEM_SYNC_DOMAIN_COUNT](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cuda-driver-api/group__CUDA__TYPES.html#group__CUDA__TYPES_1gge12b8a782bebe21b1ac0091bf9f4e2a3e21f4ac335f51cc411f8059a1348274c).

default_.doc: The default domain ID to use for designated kernels.

remote.doc: The remote domain ID to use for designated kernels.

flags.doc: CUmemProt accessibility flags to set on the request.

location.doc: Location on which the request is to change it's accessibility.

CUmemAllocationProp_v1.doc: Specifies the allocation properties for a allocation.

compressionType.doc:
Allocation hint for requesting compressible memory. On devices that support Compute Data Compression, compressible memory
can be used to accelerate accesses to data with unstructured sparsity and other compressible data patterns. Applications are
expected to query allocation property of the handle obtained with `cuMemCreate` using `cuMemGetAllocationPropertiesFromHandle` to validate if the obtained allocation is compressible or not. Note that compressed memory may not be mappable on all devices.

usage.doc: Bitmask indicating intended usage for this allocation.

win32HandleMetaData.doc:
Windows-specific POBJECT_ATTRIBUTES required when [CU_MEM_HANDLE_TYPE_WIN32](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cuda-driver-api/group__CUDA__TYPES.html#group__CUDA__TYPES_1gg450a23153d86fce0afe30e25d63caef9439b7704f58e569543c4b60038cc251e) is specified. This object attributes structure includes security attributes that define the scope of which exported allocations
may be transferred to other processes. In all other cases, this field is required to be zero.

CUmemFabricHandle_v1.doc:
Fabric handle - An opaque handle representing a memory allocation that can be exported to processes in same or different nodes.
For IPC between processes on different nodes they must be connected via the NVSwitch fabric.

type.doc: Specifies the location type, which modifies the meaning of id.

CUmemPoolProps_v1.doc: Specifies the properties of allocations made from the pool.

allocType.doc: Allocation type. Currently must be specified as [`CUmemAllocationType::CU_MEM_ALLOCATION_TYPE_PINNED`].

handleTypes.doc: Handle types that will be supported by allocations from the pool.

maxSize.doc: Maximum pool size. When set to 0, defaults to a system dependent value.

reserved.doc: reserved for future use, must be 0.

usage.doc: Bitmask indicating intended usage for the pool.

win32SecurityAttributes.doc:
Windows-specific LPSECURITYATTRIBUTES required when [CU_MEM_HANDLE_TYPE_WIN32](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cuda-driver-api/group__CUDA__TYPES.html#group__CUDA__TYPES_1gg450a23153d86fce0afe30e25d63caef9439b7704f58e569543c4b60038cc251e) is specified. This security attribute defines the scope of which exported allocations may be transferred to other processes.
In all other cases, this field is required to be zero.

CUmemPoolPtrExportData_v1.doc: Opaque data for exporting a pool allocation.

CUmemcpy3DOperand_v1.doc: Struct representing an operand for copy with `cuMemcpy3DBatchAsync`.

layerHeight.doc: Height of each layer in elements.

locHint.doc: Hint location for the operand. Ignored when the pointers are not managed memory or memory allocated outside CUDA.

offset.doc: offset into the array in elements.

ptr.doc: Struct representing an operand when CUmemcpy3DOperand::type is [CU_MEMCPY_OPERAND_TYPE_POINTER](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cuda-driver-api/group__CUDA__TYPES.html#group__CUDA__TYPES_1gg507c7c67580a9b998fd8a59ce883c7d4c8f57f3e6c8b3863359d15cf89aaa593).

rowLength.doc: Length of each row in elements.

CUmemcpyAttributes_v1.doc: Attributes specific to copies within a batch. For more details on usage see `cuMemcpyBatchAsync`.

dstLocHint.doc: Hint location for the destination operand. Ignored when the pointers are not managed memory or memory allocated outside CUDA.

flags.doc: Additional flags for copies with this attribute. See `CUmemcpyFlags`.

srcAccessOrder.doc: Source access ordering to be observed for copies with this attribute.

srcLocHint.doc: Hint location for the source operand. Ignored when the pointers are not managed memory or memory allocated outside CUDA.

CUmulticastObjectProp_v1.doc: Specifies the properties for a multicast object.

flags.doc: Flags for future use, must be zero now.

handleTypes.doc: Bitmask of exportable handle types (see `CUmemAllocationHandleType`) for this object.

numDevices.doc: The number of devices in the multicast team that will bind memory to this object.

size.doc: The maximum amount of memory that can be bound to this multicast object per device.

operation.doc: Operation. This is the first field of all the union elemets and acts as a TAG to determine which union member is valid.

CUtensorMap.doc: Tensor map descriptor. Requires compiler support for aligning to 128 bytes.

CUDA_ARRAY3D_COLOR_ATTACHMENT.doc: This flag indicates that the CUDA array may be bound as a color target in an external graphics API.

CUDA_ARRAY3D_CUBEMAP.doc:
If set, the CUDA array is a collection of six 2D arrays, representing faces of a cube. The width of such a CUDA array must
be equal to its height, and Depth must be six. If `CUDA_ARRAY3D_LAYERED` flag is also set, then the CUDA array is a collection of cubemaps and Depth must be a multiple of six.

CUDA_ARRAY3D_DEFERRED_MAPPING.doc: This flag if set indicates that the CUDA array or CUDA mipmapped array will allow deferred memory mapping.

CUDA_ARRAY3D_DEPTH_TEXTURE.doc: This flag if set indicates that the CUDA array is a DEPTH_TEXTURE.

CUDA_ARRAY3D_LAYERED.doc:
If set, the CUDA array is a collection of layers, where each layer is either a 1D or a 2D array and the Depth member of CUDA_ARRAY3D_DESCRIPTOR
specifies the number of layers, not the depth of a 3D array.

CUDA_ARRAY3D_SPARSE.doc: This flag if set indicates that the CUDA array or CUDA mipmapped array is a sparse CUDA array or CUDA mipmapped array respectively.

CUDA_ARRAY3D_SURFACE_LDST.doc: This flag must be set in order to bind a surface reference to the CUDA array.

CUDA_ARRAY3D_TEXTURE_GATHER.doc: This flag must be set in order to perform texture gather operations on a CUDA array.

CUDA_ARRAY3D_VIDEO_ENCODE_DECODE.doc: This flag indicates that the CUDA array will be used for hardware accelerated video encode/decode operations.

CUDA_COOPERATIVE_LAUNCH_MULTI_DEVICE_NO_.doc: If set, any subsequent work pushed in a stream that participated in a call to `cuLaunchCooperativeKernelMultiDevice` will only wait for the kernel launched on the GPU corresponding to that stream to complete before it begins execution.
If set, each kernel launched as part of `cuLaunchCooperativeKernelMultiDevice` only waits for prior work in the stream corresponding to that GPU to complete before the kernel begins execution.

CUDA_EGL_INFINITE_TIMEOUT.doc: Indicates that timeout for `cuEGLStreamConsumerAcquireFrame` is infinite.

CUDA_EXTERNAL_MEMORY_DEDICATED.doc: Indicates that the external memory object is a dedicated resource.

CUDA_EXTERNAL_SEMAPHORE_SIGNAL_SKIP_NVSC.doc:
When the flags parameter of CUDA_EXTERNAL_SEMAPHORE_SIGNAL_PARAMS contains this flag, it indicates that signaling an external semaphore
object should skip performing appropriate memory synchronization operations over all the external memory objects that are
imported as CU_EXTERNAL_MEMORY_HANDLE_TYPE_NVSCIBUF, which otherwise are performed by default to ensure data coherency with other importers of the same NvSciBuf memory objects.

CUDA_EXTERNAL_SEMAPHORE_WAIT_SKIP_NVSCIB.doc:
When the flags parameter of CUDA_EXTERNAL_SEMAPHORE_WAIT_PARAMS contains this flag, it indicates that waiting on an external semaphore object
should skip performing appropriate memory synchronization operations over all the external memory objects that are imported
as CU_EXTERNAL_MEMORY_HANDLE_TYPE_NVSCIBUF, which otherwise are performed by default to ensure data coherency with other importers of the same NvSciBuf memory objects.

CUDA_NVSCISYNC_ATTR_SIGNAL.doc: When flags of `cuDeviceGetNvSciSyncAttributes` is set to this, it indicates that application needs signaler specific NvSciSyncAttr to be filled by `cuDeviceGetNvSciSyncAttributes`.

CUDA_NVSCISYNC_ATTR_WAIT.doc: When flags of `cuDeviceGetNvSciSyncAttributes` is set to this, it indicates that application needs waiter specific NvSciSyncAttr to be filled by `cuDeviceGetNvSciSyncAttributes`.

CU_ARRAY_SPARSE_PROPERTIES_SINGLE_MIPTAI.doc: Indicates that the layered sparse CUDA array or CUDA mipmapped array has a single mip tail region for all layers.

CU_DEVICE_INVALID.doc: Device that represents an invalid device.

CU_GRAPH_COND_ASSIGN_DEFAULT.doc: Conditional node handle flags Default value is applied when graph is launched.

CU_GRAPH_KERNEL_NODE_PORT_DEFAULT.doc: This port activates when the kernel has finished executing.

CU_GRAPH_KERNEL_NODE_PORT_LAUNCH_ORDER.doc: This port activates when all blocks of the kernel have begun execution. See also CU_LAUNCH_ATTRIBUTE_LAUNCH_COMPLETION_EVENT.

CU_GRAPH_KERNEL_NODE_PORT_PROGRAMMATIC.doc: This port activates when all blocks of the kernel have performed [cudaTriggerProgrammaticLaunchCompletion()](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cuda-runtime-api/group__CUDART__EXECUTION.html#group__CUDART__EXECUTION_1ge194af462d927583bed3acf60d450218) or have terminated. It must be used with edge type CU_GRAPH_DEPENDENCY_TYPE_PROGRAMMATIC. See also CU_LAUNCH_ATTRIBUTE_PROGRAMMATIC_EVENT.

CU_LAUNCH_KERNEL_REQUIRED_BLOCK_DIM.doc: Launch with the required block dimension.

CU_LAUNCH_PARAM_BUFFER_POINTER.doc:
Indicator that the next value in the extra parameter to `cuLaunchKernel` will be a pointer to a buffer containing all kernel parameters used for launching kernel f. This buffer needs to honor all alignment/padding requirements of the individual parameters. If `CU_LAUNCH_PARAM_BUFFER_SIZE` is not also specified in the extra array, then `CU_LAUNCH_PARAM_BUFFER_POINTER` will have no effect.

###### Value

((void\*)CU_LAUNCH_PARAM_BUFFER_POINTER_AS_INT).

CU_LAUNCH_PARAM_BUFFER_POINTER_AS_INT.doc: C++ compile time constant for CU_LAUNCH_PARAM_BUFFER_POINTER.

CU_LAUNCH_PARAM_BUFFER_SIZE.doc:
Indicator that the next value in the extra parameter to `cuLaunchKernel` will be a pointer to a size_t which contains the size of the buffer specified with `CU_LAUNCH_PARAM_BUFFER_POINTER`. It is required that `CU_LAUNCH_PARAM_BUFFER_POINTER` also be specified in the extra array if the value associated with `CU_LAUNCH_PARAM_BUFFER_SIZE` is not zero.

###### Value

((void\*)CU_LAUNCH_PARAM_BUFFER_SIZE_AS_INT).

CU_LAUNCH_PARAM_BUFFER_SIZE_AS_INT.doc: C++ compile time constant for CU_LAUNCH_PARAM_BUFFER_SIZE.

CU_LAUNCH_PARAM_END.doc:
End of array terminator for the extra parameter to `cuLaunchKernel`

###### Value

((void\*)CU_LAUNCH_PARAM_END_AS_INT).

CU_LAUNCH_PARAM_END_AS_INT.doc: C++ compile time constant for CU_LAUNCH_PARAM_END.

CU_MEMHOSTALLOC_DEVICEMAP.doc: If set, host memory is mapped into CUDA address space and `cuMemHostGetDevicePointer` may be called on the host pointer. Flag for `cuMemHostAlloc`.

CU_MEMHOSTALLOC_PORTABLE.doc: If set, host memory is portable between CUDA contexts. Flag for `cuMemHostAlloc`.

CU_MEMHOSTALLOC_WRITECOMBINED.doc:
If set, host memory is allocated as write-combined - fast to write, faster to DMA, slow to read except via SSE4 streaming
load instruction (MOVNTDQA). Flag for `cuMemHostAlloc`.

CU_MEMHOSTREGISTER_DEVICEMAP.doc: If set, host memory is mapped into CUDA address space and `cuMemHostGetDevicePointer` may be called on the host pointer. Flag for `cuMemHostRegister`.

CU_MEMHOSTREGISTER_IOMEMORY.doc:
If set, the passed memory pointer is treated as pointing to some memory-mapped I/O space, e.g. belonging to a third-party
PCIe device. On Windows the flag is a no-op. On Linux that memory is marked as non cache-coherent for the GPU and is expected
to be physically contiguous. It may return CUDA_ERROR_NOT_PERMITTED if run as an unprivileged user, CUDA_ERROR_NOT_SUPPORTED on older Linux kernel versions. On all other platforms, it is not supported and CUDA_ERROR_NOT_SUPPORTED is returned. Flag for `cuMemHostRegister`.

CU_MEMHOSTREGISTER_PORTABLE.doc: If set, host memory is portable between CUDA contexts. Flag for `cuMemHostRegister`.

CU_MEMHOSTREGISTER_READ_ONLY.doc:
If set, the passed memory pointer is treated as pointing to memory that is considered read-only by the device. On platforms
without CU_DEVICE_ATTRIBUTE_PAGEABLE_MEMORY_ACCESS_USES_HOST_PAGE_TABLES, this flag is required in order to register memory mapped to the CPU as read-only. Support for the use of this flag can be
queried from the device attribute CU_DEVICE_ATTRIBUTE_READ_ONLY_HOST_REGISTER_SUPPORTED. Using this flag with a current context associated with a device that does not have this attribute set will cause `cuMemHostRegister` to error with CUDA_ERROR_NOT_SUPPORTED.

CU_MEM_CREATE_USAGE_HW_DECOMPRESS.doc: This flag, if set, indicates that the memory will be used as a buffer for hardware accelerated decompression.

CU_MEM_CREATE_USAGE_TILE_POOL.doc: This flag if set indicates that the memory will be used as a tile pool.

CU_MEM_POOL_CREATE_USAGE_HW_DECOMPRESS.doc: This flag, if set, indicates that the memory will be used as a buffer for hardware accelerated decompression.

CU_PARAM_TR_DEFAULT.doc: For texture references loaded into the module, use default texunit from texture reference.

CU_STREAM_LEGACY.doc:
Legacy stream handle

Stream handle that can be passed as a CUstream to use an implicit stream with legacy synchronization behavior.

See details of the [synchronization behavior](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cuda-driver-api/stream-sync-behavior.html#stream-sync-behavior).

CU_STREAM_PER_THREAD.doc:
Per-thread stream handle

Stream handle that can be passed as a CUstream to use an implicit stream with per-thread synchronization behavior.

See details of the [synchronization behavior](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cuda-driver-api/stream-sync-behavior.html#stream-sync-behavior).

CU_TRSA_OVERRIDE_FORMAT.doc: Override the texref format with a format inferred from the array. Flag for `cuTexRefSetArray`.

CU_TRSF_DISABLE_TRILINEAR_OPTIMIZATION.doc: Disable any trilinear filtering optimizations. Flag for `cuTexRefSetFlags` and `cuTexObjectCreate`.

CU_TRSF_NORMALIZED_COORDINATES.doc: Use normalized texture coordinates in the range 0,1) instead of [0,dim). Flag for [cuTexRefSetFlags() and `cuTexObjectCreate`.

CU_TRSF_READ_AS_INTEGER.doc: Read the texture as integers rather than promoting the values to floats in the range [0,1]. Flag for `cuTexRefSetFlags` and `cuTexObjectCreate`.

CU_TRSF_SEAMLESS_CUBEMAP.doc: Enable seamless cube map filtering. Flag for `cuTexObjectCreate`.

CU_TRSF_SRGB.doc: Perform sRGB->linear conversion during texture read. Flag for `cuTexRefSetFlags` and `cuTexObjectCreate`.

MAX_PLANES.doc: Maximum number of planes per frame.

CUdeviceptr_v2.doc:
CUDA device pointer CUdeviceptr is defined as an unsigned integer type whose size matches the size of a pointer on the target
platform.

CUgreenCtx.doc: A green context handle. This handle can be used safely from only one CPU thread at a time. Created via `cuGreenCtxCreate`.

CUoccupancyB2DSize.doc: Block size to per-block dynamic shared memory mapping for a certain kernel.

CUstreamCallback.signature: void(CUDA_CB* CUstreamCallback)(CUstream hStream, CUresult status, void* userData)

CUsurfObject.doc: An opaque value that represents a CUDA surface object.

CUsurfObject_v1.doc: An opaque value that represents a CUDA surface object.

CUtexObject.doc: An opaque value that represents a CUDA texture object.

CUtexObject_v1.doc: An opaque value that represents a CUDA texture object.

CUDA_POINTER_ATTRIBUTE_ACCESS_FLAGS.doc: Access flags that specify the level of access the current context's device has on the memory referenced.

CU_POINTER_ATTRIBUTE_ACCESS_FLAG_NONE.doc:
No access, meaning the device cannot access this memory at all, thus must be staged through accessible memory in order to
complete certain operations.

CU_POINTER_ATTRIBUTE_ACCESS_FLAG_READ.doc: Read-only access, meaning writes to this memory are considered invalid accesses and thus return error in that case.

CU_POINTER_ATTRIBUTE_ACCESS_FLAG_READWRI.doc: Read-write access, the device has full read-write access to the memory.

CUGPUDirectRDMAWritesOrdering.doc: Platform native ordering for GPUDirect RDMA writes.

CU_GPU_DIRECT_RDMA_WRITES_ORDERING_NONE.doc: The device does not natively support ordering of remote writes. `cuFlushGPUDirectRDMAWrites` can be leveraged if supported.

CU_GPU_DIRECT_RDMA_WRITES_ORDERING_OWNER.doc: Natively, the device can consistently consume remote writes, although other CUDA devices may not.

CU_GPU_DIRECT_RDMA_WRITES_ORDERING_ALL_D.doc: Any CUDA device in the system can consistently consume remote writes to this device.

CUaccessProperty.doc: Specifies performance hint with `CUaccessPolicyWindow` for hitProp and missProp members.

CU_ACCESS_PROPERTY_STREAMING.doc: Streaming access is less likely to persit from cache.

CU_ACCESS_PROPERTY_PERSISTING.doc: Persisting access is more likely to persist in cache.

CU_AD_FORMAT_BC1_UNORM.doc: 4 channel unsigned normalized block-compressed (BC1 compression) format.

CU_AD_FORMAT_BC1_UNORM_SRGB.doc: 4 channel unsigned normalized block-compressed (BC1 compression) format with sRGB encoding.

CU_AD_FORMAT_BC2_UNORM.doc: 4 channel unsigned normalized block-compressed (BC2 compression) format.

CU_AD_FORMAT_BC2_UNORM_SRGB.doc: 4 channel unsigned normalized block-compressed (BC2 compression) format with sRGB encoding.

CU_AD_FORMAT_BC3_UNORM.doc: 4 channel unsigned normalized block-compressed (BC3 compression) format.

CU_AD_FORMAT_BC3_UNORM_SRGB.doc: 4 channel unsigned normalized block-compressed (BC3 compression) format with sRGB encoding.

CU_AD_FORMAT_BC4_UNORM.doc: 1 channel unsigned normalized block-compressed (BC4 compression) format.

CU_AD_FORMAT_BC4_SNORM.doc: 1 channel signed normalized block-compressed (BC4 compression) format.

CU_AD_FORMAT_BC5_UNORM.doc: 2 channel unsigned normalized block-compressed (BC5 compression) format.

CU_AD_FORMAT_BC5_SNORM.doc: 2 channel signed normalized block-compressed (BC5 compression) format.

CU_AD_FORMAT_BC6H_UF16.doc: 3 channel unsigned half-float block-compressed (BC6H compression) format.

CU_AD_FORMAT_BC6H_SF16.doc: 3 channel signed half-float block-compressed (BC6H compression) format.

CU_AD_FORMAT_BC7_UNORM.doc: 4 channel unsigned normalized block-compressed (BC7 compression) format.

CU_AD_FORMAT_BC7_UNORM_SRGB.doc: 4 channel unsigned normalized block-compressed (BC7 compression) format with sRGB encoding.

CU_AD_FORMAT_YUY2.doc: 2 channel, 8-bit YUV packed planar format, with 4:2:2 sampling.

CU_AD_FORMAT_Y210.doc: 2 channel, 10-bit YUV packed planar format, with 4:2:2 sampling.

CU_AD_FORMAT_Y216.doc: 2 channel, 16-bit YUV packed planar format, with 4:2:2 sampling.

CU_AD_FORMAT_AYUV.doc: 4 channel, 8-bit YUV packed planar format, with 4:4:4 sampling.

CU_AD_FORMAT_Y410.doc: 10-bit YUV packed planar format, with 4:4:4 sampling.

CU_AD_FORMAT_Y416.doc: 4 channel, 12-bit YUV packed planar format, with 4:4:4 sampling.

CU_AD_FORMAT_Y444_PLANAR8.doc: 3 channel 8-bit YUV planar format, with 4:4:4 sampling.

CU_AD_FORMAT_Y444_PLANAR10.doc: 3 channel 10-bit YUV planar format, with 4:4:4 sampling.

CU_AD_FORMAT_YUV444_8bit_SemiPlanar.doc: 3 channel 8-bit YUV semi-planar format, with 4:4:4 sampling.

CU_AD_FORMAT_YUV444_16bit_SemiPlanar.doc: 3 channel 16-bit YUV semi-planar format, with 4:4:4 sampling.

CU_AD_FORMAT_UINT8_PACKED_422.doc: 4 channel unsigned 8-bit YUV packed format, with 4:2:2 sampling.

CU_AD_FORMAT_UINT8_PACKED_444.doc: 4 channel unsigned 8-bit YUV packed format, with 4:4:4 sampling.

CU_AD_FORMAT_UINT8_SEMIPLANAR_420.doc: 3 channel unsigned 8-bit YUV semi-planar format, with 4:2:0 sampling.

CU_AD_FORMAT_UINT16_SEMIPLANAR_420.doc: 3 channel unsigned 16-bit YUV semi-planar format, with 4:2:0 sampling.

CU_AD_FORMAT_UINT8_SEMIPLANAR_422.doc: 3 channel unsigned 8-bit YUV semi-planar format, with 4:2:2 sampling.

CU_AD_FORMAT_UINT16_SEMIPLANAR_422.doc: 3 channel unsigned 16-bit YUV semi-planar format, with 4:2:2 sampling.

CU_AD_FORMAT_UINT8_SEMIPLANAR_444.doc: 3 channel unsigned 8-bit YUV semi-planar format, with 4:4:4 sampling.

CU_AD_FORMAT_UINT16_SEMIPLANAR_444.doc: 3 channel unsigned 16-bit YUV semi-planar format, with 4:4:4 sampling.

CU_AD_FORMAT_UINT8_PLANAR_420.doc: 3 channel unsigned 8-bit YUV planar format, with 4:2:0 sampling.

CU_AD_FORMAT_UINT16_PLANAR_420.doc: 3 channel unsigned 16-bit YUV planar format, with 4:2:0 sampling.

CU_AD_FORMAT_UINT8_PLANAR_422.doc: 3 channel unsigned 8-bit YUV planar format, with 4:2:2 sampling.

CU_AD_FORMAT_UINT16_PLANAR_422.doc: 3 channel unsigned 16-bit YUV planar format, with 4:2:2 sampling.

CU_AD_FORMAT_UINT8_PLANAR_444.doc: 3 channel unsigned 8-bit YUV planar format, with 4:4:4 sampling.

CU_AD_FORMAT_UINT16_PLANAR_444.doc: 3 channel unsigned 16-bit YUV planar format, with 4:4:4 sampling.

CUasyncNotificationType.doc: Types of async notification that can be sent.

CU_ASYNC_NOTIFICATION_TYPE_OVER_BUDGET.doc: Sent when the process has exceeded its device memory budget.

CUclusterSchedulingPolicy.doc: Cluster scheduling policies. These may be passed to `cuFuncSetAttribute` or `cuKernelSetAttribute`.

CU_CLUSTER_SCHEDULING_POLICY_SPREAD.doc: spread the blocks within a cluster to the SMs.

CU_CLUSTER_SCHEDULING_POLICY_LOAD_BALANC.doc: allow the hardware to load-balance the blocks in a cluster to the SMs.

CUeglFrameType.doc: CUDA EglFrame type - array or pointer.

CUeglResourceLocationFlags.doc:
Resource location flags- sysmem or vidmem

For CUDA context on iGPU, since video and system memory are equivalent - these flags will not have an effect on the execution.

For CUDA context on dGPU, applications can use the flag `CUeglResourceLocationFlags` to give a hint about the desired location.

CU_EGL_RESOURCE_LOCATION_SYSMEM - the frame data is made resident on the system memory to be accessed by CUDA.

CU_EGL_RESOURCE_LOCATION_VIDMEM - the frame data is made resident on the dedicated video memory to be accessed by CUDA.

There may be an additional latency due to new allocation and data migration, if the frame is produced on a different memory.

CU_EVENT_DISABLE_TIMING.doc: Event will not record timing data.

CU_EVENT_INTERPROCESS.doc: Event is suitable for interprocess use. [`CUevent_flags::CU_EVENT_DISABLE_TIMING`] must be set.

CU_EVENT_RECORD_EXTERNAL.doc:
When using stream capture, create an event record node instead of the default behavior. This flag is invalid when used outside
of capture.

CU_EVENT_SCHED_BLOCKING_SYNC.doc: Set blocking synchronization as default scheduling.

CU_EVENT_WAIT_EXTERNAL.doc:
When using stream capture, create an event wait node instead of the default behavior. This flag is invalid when used outside
of capture.

CU_EXEC_AFFINITY_TYPE_SM_COUNT.doc: Create a context with limited SMs.

CU_FLUSH_GPU_DIRECT_RDMA_WRITES_OPTION_H.doc: `cuFlushGPUDirectRDMAWrites` and its CUDA Runtime API counterpart are supported on the device.

CU_FLUSH_GPU_DIRECT_RDMA_WRITES_OPTION_M.doc: The CU_STREAM_WAIT_VALUE_FLUSH flag and the CU_STREAM_MEM_OP_FLUSH_REMOTE_WRITES MemOp are supported on the device.

CU_FLUSH_GPU_DIRECT_RDMA_WRITES_TO_OWNER.doc: Blocks until remote writes are visible to the CUDA device context owning the data.

CU_FLUSH_GPU_DIRECT_RDMA_WRITES_TO_ALL_D.doc: Blocks until remote writes are visible to all CUDA device contexts.

CU_FLUSH_GPU_DIRECT_RDMA_WRITES_TARGET_C.doc: Sets the target for `cuFlushGPUDirectRDMAWrites` to the currently active CUDA device context.

CU_FUNC_CACHE_PREFER_NONE.doc: no preference for shared memory or L1 (default).

CU_FUNC_CACHE_PREFER_SHARED.doc: prefer larger shared memory and smaller L1 cache.

CU_FUNC_CACHE_PREFER_L1.doc: prefer larger L1 cache and smaller shared memory.

CU_FUNC_CACHE_PREFER_EQUAL.doc: prefer equal sized L1 cache and shared memory.

CU_FUNC_ATTRIBUTE_MAX_THREADS_PER_BLOCK.doc:
The maximum number of threads per block, beyond which a launch of the function would fail. This number depends on both the
function and the device on which the function is currently loaded.

CU_FUNC_ATTRIBUTE_SHARED_SIZE_BYTES.doc:
The size in bytes of statically-allocated shared memory required by this function. This does not include dynamically-allocated
shared memory requested by the user at runtime.

CU_FUNC_ATTRIBUTE_CONST_SIZE_BYTES.doc: The size in bytes of user-allocated constant memory required by this function.

CU_FUNC_ATTRIBUTE_LOCAL_SIZE_BYTES.doc: The size in bytes of local memory used by each thread of this function.

CU_FUNC_ATTRIBUTE_NUM_REGS.doc: The number of registers used by each thread of this function.

CU_FUNC_ATTRIBUTE_PTX_VERSION.doc:
The PTX virtual architecture version for which the function was compiled. This value is the major PTX version \* 10 + the minor
PTX version, so a PTX version 1.3 function would return the value 13. Note that this may return the undefined value of 0 for
cubins compiled prior to CUDA 3.0.

CU_FUNC_ATTRIBUTE_BINARY_VERSION.doc:
The binary architecture version for which the function was compiled. This value is the major binary version \* 10 + the minor
binary version, so a binary version 1.3 function would return the value 13. Note that this will return a value of 10 for legacy
cubins that do not have a properly-encoded binary architecture version.

CU_FUNC_ATTRIBUTE_CACHE_MODE_CA.doc: The attribute to indicate whether the function has been compiled with user specified option "-Xptxas --dlcm=ca" set .

CU_FUNC_ATTRIBUTE_MAX_DYNAMIC_SHARED_SIZ.doc:
The maximum size in bytes of dynamically-allocated shared memory that can be used by this function. If the user-specified
dynamic shared memory size is larger than this value, the launch will fail. The default value of this attribute is CU_DEVICE_ATTRIBUTE_MAX_SHARED_MEMORY_PER_BLOCK - CU_FUNC_ATTRIBUTE_SHARED_SIZE_BYTES, except when CU_FUNC_ATTRIBUTE_SHARED_SIZE_BYTES is greater than CU_DEVICE_ATTRIBUTE_MAX_SHARED_MEMORY_PER_BLOCK, then the default value of this attribute is 0. The value can be increased to CU_DEVICE_ATTRIBUTE_MAX_SHARED_MEMORY_PER_BLOCK_OPTIN - CU_FUNC_ATTRIBUTE_SHARED_SIZE_BYTES. See `cuFuncSetAttribute`, `cuKernelSetAttribute`.

CU_FUNC_ATTRIBUTE_PREFERRED_SHARED_MEMOR.doc:
On devices where the L1 cache and shared memory use the same hardware resources, this sets the shared memory carveout preference,
in percent of the total shared memory. Refer to CU_DEVICE_ATTRIBUTE_MAX_SHARED_MEMORY_PER_MULTIPROCESSOR. This is only a hint, and the driver can choose a different ratio if required to execute the function. See `cuFuncSetAttribute`, `cuKernelSetAttribute`.

CU_FUNC_ATTRIBUTE_CLUSTER_SIZE_MUST_BE_S.doc: If this attribute is set, the kernel must launch with a valid cluster size specified. See `cuFuncSetAttribute`, `cuKernelSetAttribute`.

CU_FUNC_ATTRIBUTE_REQUIRED_CLUSTER_WIDTH.doc:
The required cluster width in blocks. The values must either all be 0 or all be positive. The validity of the cluster dimensions
is otherwise checked at launch time.If the value is set during compile time, it cannot be set at runtime. Setting it at runtime
will return [`CUresult::CUDA_ERROR_NOT_PERMITTED`]. See `cuFuncSetAttribute`, `cuKernelSetAttribute`.

CU_FUNC_ATTRIBUTE_REQUIRED_CLUSTER_HEIGH.doc:
The required cluster height in blocks. The values must either all be 0 or all be positive. The validity of the cluster dimensions
is otherwise checked at launch time.If the value is set during compile time, it cannot be set at runtime. Setting it at runtime
should return [`CUresult::CUDA_ERROR_NOT_PERMITTED`]. See `cuFuncSetAttribute`, `cuKernelSetAttribute`.

CU_FUNC_ATTRIBUTE_REQUIRED_CLUSTER_DEPTH.doc:
The required cluster depth in blocks. The values must either all be 0 or all be positive. The validity of the cluster dimensions
is otherwise checked at launch time.If the value is set during compile time, it cannot be set at runtime. Setting it at runtime
should return [`CUresult::CUDA_ERROR_NOT_PERMITTED`]. See `cuFuncSetAttribute`, `cuKernelSetAttribute`.

CU_FUNC_ATTRIBUTE_NON_PORTABLE_CLUSTER_S.doc:
Whether the function can be launched with non-portable cluster size. 1 is allowed, 0 is disallowed. A non-portable cluster
size may only function on the specific SKUs the program is tested on. The launch might fail if the program is run on a different
hardware platform.CUDA API provides cudaOccupancyMaxActiveClusters to assist with checking whether the desired size can be
launched on the current device.Portable Cluster SizeA portable cluster size is guaranteed to be functional on all compute
capabilities higher than the target compute capability. The portable cluster size for sm_90 is 8 blocks per cluster. This
value may increase for future compute capabilities.The specific hardware unit may support higher cluster sizes that’s not
guaranteed to be portable. See `cuFuncSetAttribute`, `cuKernelSetAttribute`.

CU_FUNC_ATTRIBUTE_CLUSTER_SCHEDULING_POL.doc:
The block scheduling policy of a function. The value type is CUclusterSchedulingPolicy / cudaClusterSchedulingPolicy. See
`cuFuncSetAttribute`, `cuKernelSetAttribute`.

CU_FUNC_ATTRIBUTE_DEVICE_NODE_UPDATE_SUP.doc: Whether the function can be updated on device. 1 means device node update is supported, 0 is unsupported. See `cuFuncGetAttribute`.

CU_GRAPH_CHILD_GRAPH_OWNERSHIP_CLONE.doc:
Default behavior for a child graph node. Child graph is cloned into the parent and memory allocation/free nodes can't be present
in the child graph.

CU_GRAPH_CHILD_GRAPH_OWNERSHIP_MOVE.doc:
The child graph is moved to the parent. The handle to the child graph is owned by the parent and will be destroyed when the
```text
parent is destroyed.The following restrictions apply to child graphs after they have been moved: Cannot be independently instantiated
or destroyed; Cannot be added as a child graph of a separate parent graph; Cannot be used as an argument to cuGraphExecUpdate;
Cannot have additional memory allocation or free nodes added.
```

CU_GRAPH_CHILD_GRAPH_OWNERSHIP_INVALID.doc: Invalid ownership flag. Set when params are queried to prevent accidentally reusing the driver-owned graph object.

CU_GRAPH_COND_TYPE_IF.doc: Conditional 'if/else' Node. Body[0] executed if condition is non-zero. If size == 2, an optional ELSE graph is created and this is executed if the condition is zero.

CU_GRAPH_COND_TYPE_WHILE.doc: Conditional 'while' Node. Body executed repeatedly while condition value is non-zero.

CU_GRAPH_COND_TYPE_SWITCH.doc:
Conditional 'switch' Node. Body[n] is executed once, where 'n' is the value of the condition. If the condition does not match
a body index, no body is launched.

CU_GRAPH_DEBUG_DOT_FLAGS_VERBOSE.doc: Output all debug data as if every debug flag is enabled.

CU_GRAPH_DEBUG_DOT_FLAGS_RUNTIME_TYPES.doc: Use CUDA Runtime structures for output.

CU_GRAPH_DEBUG_DOT_FLAGS_EVENT_NODE_PARA.doc: Adds CUevent handle from record and wait nodes to output.

CU_GRAPH_DEBUG_DOT_FLAGS_HANDLES.doc: Adds node handles and every kernel function handle to output.

CU_GRAPH_DEBUG_DOT_FLAGS_MEM_ALLOC_NODE_.doc: Adds memory alloc node parameters to output.

CU_GRAPH_DEBUG_DOT_FLAGS_MEM_FREE_NODE_P.doc: Adds memory free node parameters to output.

CU_GRAPH_DEBUG_DOT_FLAGS_BATCH_MEM_OP_NO.doc: Adds batch mem op node parameters to output.

CU_GRAPH_DEBUG_DOT_FLAGS_CONDITIONAL_NOD.doc: Adds conditional node parameters to output.

CUgraphDependencyType.doc: Type annotations that can be applied to graph edges as part of `CUgraphEdgeData`.

CU_GRAPH_DEPENDENCY_TYPE_PROGRAMMATIC.doc: This dependency type allows the downstream node to use <cudaGridDependencySynchronize()>. It may only be used between kernel nodes, and must be used with either the `CU_GRAPH_KERNEL_NODE_PORT_PROGRAMMATIC` or `CU_GRAPH_KERNEL_NODE_PORT_LAUNCH_ORDER` outgoing port.

CU_GRAPH_EXEC_UPDATE_ERROR.doc: The update failed for an unexpected reason which is described in the return value of the function.

CU_GRAPH_EXEC_UPDATE_ERROR_TOPOLOGY_CHAN.doc: The update failed because the topology changed.

CU_GRAPH_EXEC_UPDATE_ERROR_NODE_TYPE_CHA.doc: The update failed because a node type changed.

CU_GRAPH_EXEC_UPDATE_ERROR_FUNCTION_CHAN.doc: The update failed because the function of a kernel node changed (CUDA driver < 11.2).

CU_GRAPH_EXEC_UPDATE_ERROR_PARAMETERS_CH.doc: The update failed because the parameters changed in a way that is not supported.

CU_GRAPH_EXEC_UPDATE_ERROR_NOT_SUPPORTED.doc: The update failed because something about the node is not supported.

CU_GRAPH_EXEC_UPDATE_ERROR_UNSUPPORTED_F.doc: The update failed because the function of a kernel node changed in an unsupported way.

CU_GRAPH_EXEC_UPDATE_ERROR_ATTRIBUTES_CH.doc: The update failed because the node attributes changed in a way that is not supported.

CUDA_GRAPH_INSTANTIATE_ERROR.doc: Instantiation failed for an unexpected reason which is described in the return value of the function.

CUDA_GRAPH_INSTANTIATE_INVALID_STRUCTURE.doc: Instantiation failed due to invalid structure, such as cycles.

CUDA_GRAPH_INSTANTIATE_NODE_OPERATION_NO.doc: Instantiation for device launch failed because the graph contained an unsupported operation.

CUDA_GRAPH_INSTANTIATE_MULTIPLE_CTXS_NOT.doc: Instantiation for device launch failed due to the nodes belonging to different contexts.

CUDA_GRAPH_INSTANTIATE_CONDITIONAL_HANDL.doc: One or more conditional handles are not associated with conditional nodes.

CUDA_GRAPH_INSTANTIATE_FLAG_AUTO_FREE_ON.doc: Automatically free memory allocated in a graph before relaunching.

CUDA_GRAPH_INSTANTIATE_FLAG_UPLOAD.doc: Automatically upload the graph after instantiation. Only supported by `cuGraphInstantiateWithParams`. The upload will be performed using the stream provided in instantiateParams.

CUDA_GRAPH_INSTANTIATE_FLAG_DEVICE_LAUNC.doc:
Instantiate the graph to be launchable from the device. This flag can only be used on platforms which support unified addressing.
This flag cannot be used in conjunction with [`CUgraphInstantiate_flags::CUDA_GRAPH_INSTANTIATE_FLAG_AUTO_FREE_ON_LAUNCH`].

CUDA_GRAPH_INSTANTIATE_FLAG_USE_NODE_PRI.doc: Run the graph using the per-node priority attributes rather than the priority of the stream it is launched into.

CU_GRAPH_NODE_TYPE_GRAPH.doc: Node which executes an embedded graph.

CU_GRAPH_NODE_TYPE_BATCH_MEM_OP.doc: Batch MemOp Node See `cuStreamBatchMemOp` and `CUstreamBatchMemOpType` for what these nodes can do.

CU_GRAPH_NODE_TYPE_CONDITIONAL.doc:
Conditional NodeMay be used to implement a conditional execution path or loop inside of a graph. The graph(s) contained within
the body of the conditional node can be selectively executed or iterated upon based on the value of a conditional variable.Handles
must be created in advance of creating the node using `cuGraphConditionalHandleCreate`.The following restrictions apply to graphs which contain conditional nodes: The graph cannot be used in a child node. Only
one instantiation of the graph may exist at any point in time. The graph cannot be cloned.To set the control value, supply
a default value when creating the handle and/or call [cudaGraphSetConditional](https://docs.nvidia.com/cuda/cuda-runtime-api/group__CUDART__GRAPH.html#group__CUDART__GRAPH_1gde392fa316b963233219ab3caac9f1b3) from device code.

CUgraphicsMapResourceFlags.doc: Flags for mapping and unmapping interop resources.

CUgraphicsRegisterFlags.doc: Flags to register a graphics resource.

CU_IPC_MEM_LAZY_ENABLE_PEER_ACCESS.doc: Automatically enable peer access between remote devices as needed.

CU_JIT_INPUT_CUBIN.doc:
Compiled device-class-specific device code
Applicable options: none.

CU_JIT_INPUT_PTX.doc:
PTX source code
Applicable options: PTX compiler options.

CU_JIT_INPUT_FATBINARY.doc:
Bundle of multiple cubins and/or PTX of some device code
Applicable options: PTX compiler options, CU_JIT_FALLBACK_STRATEGY.

CU_JIT_INPUT_OBJECT.doc:
Host object with embedded device code
Applicable options: PTX compiler options, CU_JIT_FALLBACK_STRATEGY.

CU_JIT_INPUT_LIBRARY.doc:
Archive of host objects with embedded device code
Applicable options: PTX compiler options, CU_JIT_FALLBACK_STRATEGY.

CU_JIT_INPUT_NVVM.doc:
High-level intermediate code for link-time optimization
Applicable options: NVVM compiler options, PTX compiler options

Only valid with LTO-IR compiled with toolkits prior to CUDA 12.0.

CU_PREFER_PTX.doc: Prefer to compile ptx if exact binary match not found.

CU_PREFER_BINARY.doc: Prefer to fall back to compatible binary code if exact match not found.

CU_JIT_MAX_REGISTERS.doc:
Max number of registers that a thread may use.
Option type: unsigned int
Applies to: compiler only.

CU_JIT_THREADS_PER_BLOCK.doc:
IN: Specifies minimum number of threads per block to target compilation for
OUT: Returns the number of threads the compiler actually targeted. This restricts the resource utilization of the compiler
(e.g. max registers) such that a block with the given number of threads should be able to launch based on register limitations.
Note, this option does not currently take into account any other resource limitations, such as shared memory utilization.
Cannot be combined with CU_JIT_TARGET.
Option type: unsigned int
Applies to: compiler only.

CU_JIT_WALL_TIME.doc:
Overwrites the option value with the total wall clock time, in milliseconds, spent in the compiler and linker
Option type: float
Applies to: compiler and linker.

CU_JIT_INFO_LOG_BUFFER.doc:
Pointer to a buffer in which to print any log messages that are informational in nature (the buffer size is specified via
option CU_JIT_INFO_LOG_BUFFER_SIZE_BYTES)
Option type: char \*
Applies to: compiler and linker.

CU_JIT_INFO_LOG_BUFFER_SIZE_BYTES.doc:
IN: Log buffer size in bytes. Log messages will be capped at this size (including null terminator)
OUT: Amount of log buffer filled with messages
Option type: unsigned int
Applies to: compiler and linker.

CU_JIT_ERROR_LOG_BUFFER.doc:
Pointer to a buffer in which to print any log messages that reflect errors (the buffer size is specified via option CU_JIT_ERROR_LOG_BUFFER_SIZE_BYTES)
Option type: char \*
Applies to: compiler and linker.

CU_JIT_ERROR_LOG_BUFFER_SIZE_BYTES.doc:
IN: Log buffer size in bytes. Log messages will be capped at this size (including null terminator)
OUT: Amount of log buffer filled with messages
Option type: unsigned int
Applies to: compiler and linker.

CU_JIT_OPTIMIZATION_LEVEL.doc:
Level of optimizations to apply to generated code (0 - 4), with 4 being the default and highest level of optimizations.
Option type: unsigned int
Applies to: compiler only.

CU_JIT_TARGET_FROM_CUCONTEXT.doc:
No option value required. Determines the target based on the current attached context (default)
Option type: No option value needed
Applies to: compiler and linker.

CU_JIT_TARGET.doc:
Target is chosen based on supplied `CUjit_target`. Cannot be combined with CU_JIT_THREADS_PER_BLOCK.
Option type: unsigned int for enumerated type `CUjit_target`
Applies to: compiler and linker.

CU_JIT_FALLBACK_STRATEGY.doc:
Specifies choice of fallback strategy if matching cubin is not found. Choice is based on supplied `CUjit_fallback`. This option cannot be used with cuLink\* APIs as the linker requires exact matches.
Option type: unsigned int for enumerated type `CUjit_fallback`
Applies to: compiler only.

CU_JIT_GENERATE_DEBUG_INFO.doc:
Specifies whether to create debug information in output (-g) (0: false, default)
Option type: int
Applies to: compiler and linker.

CU_JIT_LOG_VERBOSE.doc:
Generate verbose log messages (0: false, default)
Option type: int
Applies to: compiler and linker.

CU_JIT_GENERATE_LINE_INFO.doc:
Generate line number information (-lineinfo) (0: false, default)
Option type: int
Applies to: compiler only.

CU_JIT_CACHE_MODE.doc:
Specifies whether to enable caching explicitly (-dlcm)
Choice is based on supplied CUjit_cacheMode_enum.
Option type: unsigned int for enumerated type CUjit_cacheMode_enum
Applies to: compiler only.

CU_JIT_FAST_COMPILE.doc: This jit option is used for internal purpose only.

CU_JIT_GLOBAL_SYMBOL_NAMES.doc:
Array of device symbol names that will be relocated to the corresponding host addresses stored in CU_JIT_GLOBAL_SYMBOL_ADDRESSES.
Must contain CU_JIT_GLOBAL_SYMBOL_COUNT entries.
When loading a device module, driver will relocate all encountered unresolved symbols to the host addresses.
It is only allowed to register symbols that correspond to unresolved global variables.
It is illegal to register the same device symbol at multiple addresses.
Option type: const char \*\*
Applies to: dynamic linker only.

CU_JIT_GLOBAL_SYMBOL_ADDRESSES.doc:
Array of host addresses that will be used to relocate corresponding device symbols stored in CU_JIT_GLOBAL_SYMBOL_NAMES.
Must contain CU_JIT_GLOBAL_SYMBOL_COUNT entries.
Option type: void \*\*
Applies to: dynamic linker only.

CU_JIT_GLOBAL_SYMBOL_COUNT.doc:
Number of entries in CU_JIT_GLOBAL_SYMBOL_NAMES and CU_JIT_GLOBAL_SYMBOL_ADDRESSES arrays.
Option type: unsigned int
Applies to: dynamic linker only.

CU_JIT_LTO.doc:
Enable link-time optimization (-dlto) for device code (Disabled by default).
This option is not supported on 32-bit platforms.
Option type: int
Applies to: compiler and linker

Only valid with LTO-IR compiled with toolkits prior to CUDA 12.0.

CU_JIT_FTZ.doc:
Control single-precision denormals (-ftz) support (0: false, default). 1 : flushes denormal values to zero 0 : preserves denormal
values Option type: int
Applies to: link-time optimization specified with [`CUjit_option::CU_JIT_LTO`]

Only valid with LTO-IR compiled with toolkits prior to CUDA 12.0.

CU_JIT_PREC_DIV.doc:
Control single-precision floating-point division and reciprocals (-prec-div) support (1: true, default). 1 : Enables the IEEE
round-to-nearest mode 0 : Enables the fast approximation mode Option type: int
Applies to: link-time optimization specified with [`CUjit_option::CU_JIT_LTO`]

Only valid with LTO-IR compiled with toolkits prior to CUDA 12.0.

CU_JIT_PREC_SQRT.doc:
Control single-precision floating-point square root (-prec-sqrt) support (1: true, default). 1 : Enables the IEEE round-to-nearest
mode 0 : Enables the fast approximation mode Option type: int
Applies to: link-time optimization specified with [`CUjit_option::CU_JIT_LTO`]

Only valid with LTO-IR compiled with toolkits prior to CUDA 12.0.

CU_JIT_FMA.doc:
Enable/Disable the contraction of floating-point multiplies and adds/subtracts into floating-point multiply-add (-fma) operations
```text
(1: Enable, default; 0: Disable). Option type: int
Applies to: link-time optimization specified with [`CUjit_option::CU_JIT_LTO`]

Only valid with LTO-IR compiled with toolkits prior to CUDA 12.0
```

CU_JIT_REFERENCED_KERNEL_NAMES.doc:
Array of kernel names that should be preserved at link time while others can be removed.
Must contain CU_JIT_REFERENCED_KERNEL_COUNT entries.
Note that kernel names can be mangled by the compiler in which case the mangled name needs to be specified.
Wildcard "\*" can be used to represent zero or more characters instead of specifying the full or mangled name.
It is important to note that the wildcard "\*" is also added implicitly. For example, specifying "foo" will match "foobaz",
"barfoo", "barfoobaz" and thus preserve all kernels with those names. This can be avoided by providing a more specific name
like "barfoobaz".
Option type: const char \*\*
Applies to: dynamic linker only

Only valid with LTO-IR compiled with toolkits prior to CUDA 12.0.

CU_JIT_REFERENCED_KERNEL_COUNT.doc:
Number of entries in CU_JIT_REFERENCED_KERNEL_NAMES array.
Option type: unsigned int
Applies to: dynamic linker only

Only valid with LTO-IR compiled with toolkits prior to CUDA 12.0.

CU_JIT_REFERENCED_VARIABLE_NAMES.doc:
Array of variable names (__device__ and/or __constant__) that should be preserved at link time while others can be removed.
Must contain CU_JIT_REFERENCED_VARIABLE_COUNT entries.
Note that variable names can be mangled by the compiler in which case the mangled name needs to be specified.
Wildcard "\*" can be used to represent zero or more characters instead of specifying the full or mangled name.
It is important to note that the wildcard "\*" is also added implicitly. For example, specifying "foo" will match "foobaz",
"barfoo", "barfoobaz" and thus preserve all variables with those names. This can be avoided by providing a more specific name
like "barfoobaz".
Option type: const char \*\*
Applies to: link-time optimization specified with [`CUjit_option::CU_JIT_LTO`]

Only valid with LTO-IR compiled with toolkits prior to CUDA 12.0.

CU_JIT_REFERENCED_VARIABLE_COUNT.doc:
Number of entries in CU_JIT_REFERENCED_VARIABLE_NAMES array.
Option type: unsigned int
Applies to: link-time optimization specified with [`CUjit_option::CU_JIT_LTO`]

Only valid with LTO-IR compiled with toolkits prior to CUDA 12.0.

CU_JIT_OPTIMIZE_UNUSED_DEVICE_VARIABLES.doc:
This option serves as a hint to enable the JIT compiler/linker to remove constant (__constant__) and device (__device__) variables
unreferenced in device code (Disabled by default).
Note that host references to constant and device variables using APIs like `cuModuleGetGlobal` with this option specified may result in undefined behavior unless the variables are explicitly specified using CU_JIT_REFERENCED_VARIABLE_NAMES.
Option type: int
Applies to: link-time optimization specified with [`CUjit_option::CU_JIT_LTO`]

Only valid with LTO-IR compiled with toolkits prior to CUDA 12.0.

CU_JIT_POSITION_INDEPENDENT_CODE.doc:
Generate position independent code (0: false)
Option type: int
Applies to: compiler only.

CU_JIT_MIN_CTA_PER_SM.doc:
This option hints to the JIT compiler the minimum number of CTAs from the kernel’s grid to be mapped to a SM. This option
is ignored when used together with CU_JIT_MAX_REGISTERS or CU_JIT_THREADS_PER_BLOCK. Optimizations based on this option need CU_JIT_MAX_THREADS_PER_BLOCK to be specified as well. For kernels already using PTX directive .minnctapersm, this option will be ignored by default. Use
CU_JIT_OVERRIDE_DIRECTIVE_VALUES to let this option take precedence over the PTX directive. Option type: unsigned int
Applies to: compiler only.

CU_JIT_MAX_THREADS_PER_BLOCK.doc:
Maximum number threads in a thread block, computed as the product of the maximum extent specifed for each dimension of the
block. This limit is guaranteed not to be exeeded in any invocation of the kernel. Exceeding the maximum number of threads
results in runtime error or kernel launch failure. For kernels already using PTX directive .maxntid, this option will be ignored
by default. Use CU_JIT_OVERRIDE_DIRECTIVE_VALUES to let this option take precedence over the PTX directive. Option type: int
Applies to: compiler only.

CU_JIT_OVERRIDE_DIRECTIVE_VALUES.doc:
This option lets the values specified using CU_JIT_MAX_REGISTERS, CU_JIT_THREADS_PER_BLOCK, CU_JIT_MAX_THREADS_PER_BLOCK and CU_JIT_MIN_CTA_PER_SM take precedence over any PTX directives. (0: Disable, default; 1: Enable) Option type: int
Applies to: compiler only.

CU_JIT_SPLIT_COMPILE.doc:
This option specifies the maximum number of concurrent threads to use when running compiler optimizations. If the specified
value is 1, the option will be ignored. If the specified value is 0, the number of threads will match the number of CPUs on
the underlying machine. Otherwise, if the option is N, then up to N threads will be used. Option type: unsigned int
Applies to: compiler only.

CU_JIT_BINARY_LOADER_THREAD_COUNT.doc:
This option specifies the maximum number of concurrent threads to use when compiling device code. If the specified value is
```text
1, the option will be ignored. If the specified value is 0, the number of threads will match the number of CPUs on the underlying
machine. Otherwise, if the option is N, then up to N threads will be used. This option is ignored if the env var CUDA_BINARY_LOADER_THREAD_COUNT
is set. Option type: unsigned int
Applies to: compiler and linker
```

CU_TARGET_COMPUTE_121.doc: Compute device class 12.1. Compute device class 9.0. with accelerated features.

CU_TARGET_COMPUTE_90A.doc: Compute device class 10.0. with accelerated features.

CU_TARGET_COMPUTE_100A.doc: Compute device class 11.0 with accelerated features.

CU_TARGET_COMPUTE_110A.doc: Compute device class 10.3. with accelerated features.

CU_TARGET_COMPUTE_103A.doc: Compute device class 12.0. with accelerated features.

CU_TARGET_COMPUTE_120A.doc: Compute device class 12.1. with accelerated features.

CU_TARGET_COMPUTE_121A.doc: Compute device class 10.x with family features.

CU_TARGET_COMPUTE_100F.doc: Compute device class 11.0 with family features.

CU_TARGET_COMPUTE_110F.doc: Compute device class 10.3. with family features.
